comment: JCS RFC 8785 cross-language parity vectors. Rust reads this file in pack::tests::jcs_cross_lang_parity; TypeScript reads the SAME file in web/src/workflow/__tests__/pack_digest.test.ts. Both compute BLAKE3(<domain> 0x00 <JCS(value)>) and must produce the byte-identical digest below. Adverse cases on purpose: key ordering by UTF-16 code unit — including the discriminant U+FFFF-vs-emoji vector, where code-point order and UTF-16 code-unit order DISAGREE (RFC 8785 wants the emoji first) — non-BMP keys, escapes, exponent forms (1e+21 / 1e-7 spellings), negative zero (-0.0, which RFC 8785 serialises as '0'). Non-finite floats are absent BY DESIGN: every canonicalisation door (verify AND digest_for) refuses them via the null-collapse guard. Integers beyond 2^53 are refused by the VERIFY pipeline's enforce_bounds; digest_for alone does not bound integers, which is documented on that function.
